newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CNA leaps after Wooltru buy.
newsitem.headline: CNA leaps after Wooltru buy.

text.p: Shares in South African stationary to music firm CNA Gallo leapt in late trading on Monday on better growth prospects following the firm's purchase late last week by clothing retailer Wooltru Ltd, dealers said.
CNA added over nine percent or 45 cents to a new 1997 high of 520 in brisk volume of almost 500,000 shares in an otherwise quiet market.
"(The rise) seems to be on the Wooltru buy," a stock market dealer said.
"The market seems to be looking at CNA favourably as they are keeping their profitable entertainment unit and getting rid of the slower, more pedestrian retail side," he said.
CNA-Gallo said last Thursday it had reached agreement in principle to dispose of all its interests in Central News Agency Ltd and Constantia Greetings (Pty) Ltd to Wooltru.

Earnings from CNA's entertainment Gallo division had recently overtaken those from the retail side. Major shareholder, The Premier Group Ltd said in June that it was considering unbundling the unit and splitting it.
A spokeswoman for CNA said that the firm was still trading under a cautionary announcement warning shareholders it was in talks that may effect its share price and that it would be renewed on Friday.
A further announcement about the Wooltru buy is expected to be made around August 29.
